findings.existing_code:
Dispatcher/orchestrator profiles explicitly receive the
`report_vendor_rate_limit` operation; `authorize_operation` permits those principals
findings.description: D6 says dispatcher/orchestrator profiles 'explicitly receive' `report_vendor_rate_limit`, but no artifact names the mechanism or owner. `authorize_operation` -> `policy_engine.check_operation` routes any operation outside READ/WRITE/ADMIN_ACTIONS to the profile's `allowed_operations`; that list is derived solely by `derive_allowed_operations` from `CAPABILITY_OPERATIONS`/`TRUST_DERIVED_OPERATIONS`/`UNIVERSAL_OPERATIONS` in `agents_config.py`, is a `SYNC_TRACKED_FIELD` overwritten by profile sync at boot, and an unmapped capability in agents.yaml raises ValueError. Task 1.4 declares only location/policy_vendor/catalog_vendor; no task in 1.x/2.x adds the operation to the derivation. wp-api-watchdog (task 3.1 tests 'report operation, 403') cannot write `agents_config.py` or `agents.yaml` (only wp-registry-core may), so the package that must prove the grant cannot create it and the package that can create it is not told to.
findings.resolution: Add an explicit wp-registry-core task stating how `report_vendor_rate_limit` enters `derive_allowed_operations` (new capability key or trust-derived tier) and which bundled lanes declare it; add the agents_config/profile-sync test file to wp-registry-core write_allow; state in D6 that the grant is derived, not hand-seeded, because profile sync reconciles `allowed_operations`.

findings.description: Two wp-integration gates are not executable as written. (a) mypy discovers config only from cwd; there is no repo-root pyproject.toml, so running from `cwd: '.'` drops `[tool.mypy] ignore_missing_imports = true` from `agent-coordinator/pyproject.toml` and diverges from CI (`uv run mypy src/` with working-directory agent-coordinator). (b) 'Coordinator regression' runs `pytest agent-coordinator/tests -q` with no marker filter, so `e2e` tests needing running services are included, whereas CI runs `-m "not e2e and not integration"`. Either the gate fails on the merged tree for reasons unrelated to dg-01, or it imposes a services-up precondition no package declares.
findings.resolution: Set `cwd: agent-coordinator` with `.venv/bin/python -m mypy --strict src` (or pass `--config-file agent-coordinator/pyproject.toml`); add `-m "not e2e and not integration"` to the regression gate and keep the Postgres migration gate as a separate, explicitly preconditioned step.

findings.existing_code:
- name: "Fresh migration gate"
          kind: command
          command: "agent-coordinator/.venv/bin/python -m pytest agent-coordinator/tests/integration/postgres/test_fresh_database_migration.py -q"
findings.description: Postgres-backed gates pass vacuously. `tests/integration/postgres/conftest.py` calls `pytest.skip("PostgreSQL not running")` when the DSN is unreachable, so `test_fresh_database_migration.py` (wp-registry-core and wp-integration) and the concurrent RPC tests for bounded reset, replay conflict, and compaction (task 2.3) exit 0 with zero tests executed. `expect_exit_code: 0` cannot distinguish 'atomic RPC replay/compaction verified' from 'skipped'. D1 rejects this pattern for the deployment test but the package gates do not apply the same rule.
findings.resolution: Declare a Postgres precondition for wp-registry-core and wp-integration and make skip a failure for these gates (e.g. `REQUIRE_POSTGRES=1` turning the conftest skip into `pytest.fail`, or a wrapper failing on any `skipped` in `-rs` output).

findings.existing_code:
`review_dispatcher.py` already has selected `agent_id`; its shared collector reports capacity
results exactly once.
findings.description: Model-scoped limits (D4, spec 'Model-scoped limit has an alternate model', SQL `scope='model'`) have no producer. In `review_dispatcher.py` capacity errors are consumed inside the adapter's model-fallback loop (`models_attempted` grows; `error_class=CAPACITY` is set only when every model fails). `ReviewResult` carries `vendor`, `model_used`, `models_attempted` but no `agent_id`, and D7/task 4.4 mandate 'once per result'. A run where model A returns 429 and fallback B succeeds yields a successful result with no capacity class, so the collector reports nothing and the A limit is never persisted. Nothing in tasks 4.3/4.4 states that intermediate per-model capacity failures become `scope=model` observations.
findings.resolution: State in D7 and tasks 4.3/4.4 that each capacity-classified attempt in `models_attempted` yields one `scope=model` observation for the exact `agent_id`, and that lane-scoped observations are emitted only when the final result is capacity-failed; add a collector test for the A-429/B-success case.

findings.description: The event schema and SQL contract contradict each other for `kind=probe`, and task 1.1 requires semantic parity between them. The schema requires `observation_id` and `source_agent_id` for every observation, but `vendor_probe_state` has no `observation_id` column (PK is `agent_id`) and names the producer `source`, not `source_agent_id`. D3/D4 never define a probe observation id. A parity test cannot pass against both artifacts as written.
findings.resolution: Either move `observation_id` into the `rate_limit` conditional `required` and rename SQL `source` to `source_agent_id` (or map explicitly in README), or add `observation_id`/`source_agent_id` to `vendor_probe_state` and define how watchdog generates it.

findings.description: D6 and D9 rely on bridge clients distinguishing `unknown_vendor_lane` from `vendor_registry_unavailable`, but the contract does not bind that promise: the 404/409 responses carry only `description` text and no `content` schema referencing `Problem`, so parity tests cannot assert the body; `vendor_registry_unavailable` appears in the enum but no path or status code emits it (no 503 anywhere); and the coordinator's existing problem+json handlers emit RFC 7807 `type/title/status/detail` with the reason in a `urn:` `type`, not a `code` field. The bridge today maps every 404 to `route_unavailable`, so without a bound body schema the older-coordinator vs bad-lane distinction has no deterministic wire form.
findings.resolution: Attach `content: application/problem+json: schema Problem` to every 4xx/5xx response on the three routes, add the response (e.g. 503) carrying `vendor_registry_unavailable`, and either adopt the existing RFC 7807 fields plus `code` or state that these routes intentionally use the flat `{detail, code}` shape.

findings.existing_code:
WHEN a legacy `vendor_limit:<policy_vendor>:<reason>` outcome has no
`dispatch_agent_id` in context
findings.description: `dispatch_agent_id` has readers but no writer. The orchestrator reads it from `context` to choose exact-lane vs legacy provider-scope handling, D8 says policy returns `to_agent_id`, and D7 says `provider_dispatch.py` gains an optional `agent_id` never inferred from provider. No artifact states who places the selected lane into the orchestrator `context` for the next dispatch or into `PhaseDispatchPayload.agent_id` (today the payload is only constructed by tests and the smoke script; the orchestrator's `dispatch_fn` is injected by the prompt layer). Without a named writer every roadmap limit takes the ambiguous legacy path and the exact-attribution scenarios in wp-roadmap-policy are dead code in production.
findings.resolution: Assign an owner: task 5.6 'orchestrator writes `context["dispatch_agent_id"] = decision.to_agent_id` on switch and the roadmap prompt layer seeds it from the initial lane selection'; task 4.4 'callers building `PhaseDispatchPayload` pass `agent_id` from that context'. If the prompt layer (SKILL.md) is the writer, add it to a package write_allow.

findings.description: D5 requires a future `reset_at` but allows `retry_after_seconds: 0`, which normalizes to `reset_at == receipt time`; under D4's `now >= reset_at` is expired rule the observation is accepted (202, stored, audited) and immediately inert. The two reset inputs have different validity rules for the same instant.
findings.resolution: Set `minimum: 1`, or state that 0 is rejected with 400 like a non-future `reset_at`.

findings.description: `dispatchable` is a required `VendorLane` field and the spec lists 'dispatchability', but neither design nor spec defines it or its relation to `availability.available` (adapter configured? transport reachable? available and not limited?). Two implementers can produce different, both-'correct' values, and D8 does not say whether the roadmap filter chain uses it.
findings.resolution: Define `dispatchable` in D2 or D4 (suggest: static, true iff the lane has at least one configured dispatch adapter/mode; independent of live state) and state whether D8 candidate filtering uses it.

findings.existing_code:
Catalog model membership is the
deterministic union of authored CLI/SDK models and the existing provider model map
findings.description: Latent join gap for local lanes: dg-00's `LocalEndpointService.sync_from_agents_config` registers an `endpoint_kind=local` lane in `model_catalog` with `vendor=agent.type` and `model=agent.sdk.model or agent.name`. A local lane without `sdk.model` is catalogued under its lane name, which is not in the 'authored CLI/SDK ∪ provider map' set, so the D4 step-2 local gate would always report it unknown/unavailable. No bundled lane currently sets `endpoint_kind: local`, so this is unreachable today, but dg-04 will add them.
findings.resolution: Note in D2 that local lanes must author `sdk.model` to be joinable, or include the dg-00 lane-name fallback in the membership union explicitly.
